task2.title: Discussion & Opinion: Sedentary Lifestyles and Modern Technology
task2.text:
Over the past dacade, modern lifestyles in many countires have transformed significantly due to rapid technological innovation. While some people argue that these developments have improved our standard of living, others believe that sedentary habits are exerting a dangerious influence on public well-bieng. In my opinion, although technological convenience offers evident advantages, the physical drawbacks outweight the conveniences if people fail to regulate their daily routines.

On the one hand, contemporary society has become increasingly reliant on digital automation. Consequentely, physical exertion during working hours has diminished drastically. Many professionals spend extensive periods dinning in front of computer screens or ordering fast food rather than preparing fresh meals at home. These habits frequently lead to excessive intake of calaries without sufficient physical exercise to burn them off. Furthermore, educational cources in primary schools often neglect physical recreation in favor of academic screen time, which prevents young learners from establishing healthy habits early in life.

On the other hand, technology has also provided individuals with valuable instruments to monitor their fitness. Smart watches and digital applications allow users to track their daily activities, which can encourage a more proactive attitude toward personal health. Nevertheless, the presence of these tools does not guarantee that people will act upon the information they receive. In fact, relying solely on electronic notifications often fail to produce meaningful behavioural changes, as true discipline requires conscious effort rather than automated reminders.

Overal, it is clear that sedentary habits have created serious obstacles for global health. Although technological advancements have simplified everyday tasks, authorities and individuals must collaborate to promote active routines before lifestyle diseases become uncontrollable.

task2.title: Agree / Disagree: Consumerism and Cheap Manufactured Goods
task2.text:
In recent years, modern buisnesses have accelerated the production and promotion of inexpensive consumer goods, particularly in the fashion and retail industries. While affordable commodities allow people from diverse financial backgrounds to purchase new items regularly, this phenomenon has led to severe environmental and financial problems. In this essay, I will discuss why the disadvantages of excessive consumerism clearly surpass its immediate benefits.

To begin with, the culture of mass consumption imposes major financial expences on ordinary households. Aggressive marketing campaigns frequently target vulnarable demographics, such as young adolescents who struggle to differenciate between genuine necessities and fleeting trends. As a result, consumers often purchase uncessary goods on credit, which pushes them into severe debt. Despite of the initial satisfaction that shopping provides, accumulating material possessions rarely contributes to long-term happiness and often results in economic distress for families with limited budgets.

In addition to financial repercussions, relentless consumerism causes immense environmental degradation. Countless low-cost products are manufactured from poor-quality materials that are neither durable nor recylcable. When consumers discard these items after only a few uses, municipal landfills become overwhelmed, leading to severe soil and water contamination. Although some multinational corporations argue that economic growth depends of continuous purchasing, sustainable progress is hardly achieveable when natural resources are depleted at an alarming rate. Therefore, athorities must implement stricter regulations on corporate waste while actively adressing irresponsible manufacturing standards.

In conclusion, cheap mass-produced goods provide superficial benefits to consumers, but the accompanying financial instability and ecological destruction represent far greater risks. Governments and citizens must prioritize sustainability over immediate economic profit.
